details:
# Issue:

With the AVM Update to the Avatars Tab in the Main Menu all the previous options were moved to "My Avatars".

My Avatars is missing quite a lot of features compared to live:

- No more "compact view"

- You can no longer sort the different categories (e.g. Date Added, Last Updated, Name, Recently Used, Performance)

- Minimizing the navigation panel removes the categories all together instead of making them icons

In general the new Avatars UI feels very weird and not coherent with the rest of the Menu.

# Expected Behaviour / Suggestion:

These missing features should be reimplemented to prevent this being a regression compared to live.

"My Avatars" should have imo just looked like it currently does on live with a "Purchased" category edited to it. Currently it just looks really out of place.

# Attachments:

Here are screenshots comparing the two:
title: [1628][AVM] "My Avatars" section has lost a lot of features compared to live

comments.value: unsure who this image is from, but it is a prime example of this issue. the same avatar with minor texture changes being listed seperately leads to significantly reduced ux
Thanks for the feedback. This is high on our hit list! There's a few different ways to solve it, but we're not sure which approach we'll take yet.

Multiple variations of the same avatar should all be under one listing. Moreover, if it's just simple color changes, the avatar creator should be encouraged to integrate that into a single version utilizing the avatar's expressions menu.

As others said, there should be one listing per base, to eliminate the noise.

Take an instant to look at a practical solution that already exists in VRchat:

(pic 1) Drop-down menu of "AvatarNow" from avatar museum

Showing the base (and base's author name) as the main listing,

then either a drop-down of variations (dedicated collumn on the right?)

or a dedicted page showing listings of duplicates,

would not only reduce the noise on main listings but potentially allow separate creators to work on a same base.

As for concerns over "others working on a same base" let take another example: (pic 2) Holoearth's player economy

When people make clothing based on liscenced characters, they purchase one as part of the process to make the listing.

Here, to post a variation on an existing base you could have something similar so the original author gets a little something off people using their base in the marketplace.

The idea of adding one layer of depth to the menu may seems annoying at first, but when someone click on the base they want they are already focused on browsing for this product in particular.

I don't think they would be too annoyed with the menu transitioning to a form similar to the screenshots full of duplicates others sent

IF it is within the context of browsing variations after selecting a base.

The current problem mostly is in the context of too much noise being created around main listings, which is a different scenario.

details:
Many users have expressed various frustrations and concerns regarding the newly added Avatar Marketplace. After reading these posts, I decided to compile my thoughts into a post examining why this change has been so poorly received.

=== Why It Doesn't Make Sense ===

Avatar creators already have methods of monetizing their products outside of this marketplace. While it may be argued that the goal of providing this marketplace is accessibility, the fact of the matter is most people will not pay for an avatar that they cannot modify themselves. With a plethora of publicly available avatars, the main reason users buy avatars is for the ability to edit, rig, customize, and accessorize them as they please. This feature has limited, if not zero appeal to the vast majority of the player base. 

On the contrary, the success of the existing marketplace used by world creators to provide in-world benefits to their supporters serves as an example of a positive monetization strategy that adds to the user experience. The use of the marketplace for worlds provides an easier-to-use alternative to external providers like Ko-fi or Patreon, with the added benefit of being integrated into the VRChat SDK, unlike the alternative options. Functionally, it provides benefits to both the creator and their subscribers. With the avatar marketplace, using VRChat's internal system is objectively less functional and useful than the external providers already in use today, in that people who purchase avatars do not have access to the base model or files. Due to these factors, the successful monetization of worlds cannot be replicated with avatars; the Avatar Marketplace provides no benefit to the seller besides discoverability and is a net downgrade for the buyer.

=== Why It's So Unpopular == 

Regardless of the merit of the concept itself, the community is also upset at the removal of functionality caused by this update. The avatar menu now looks out of place in the current user interface and has had substantial portions of its functionality removed. Although it has been stated that this functionality will return, it begs the question: Why was this feature released in such an unfinished and unpolished state? And why was the existing avatar menu completely scrapped for a worse, uglier version that doesn't even work correctly? Similarly, the aggressive design choice of forcing users to view the marketplace every time they wish to interact with their avatars is off-putting and a hassle for people who regularly interact with their avatars. Although many non-intrusive implementations of this change were possible, the VRChat team inexplicably decided instead to obstruct the user experience and actively worsen the functionality and appearance of the avatar menu.

=== Nobody Wants This === 

Many ascribe this change to greed, but I feel that it's important to remember that one should never attribute to malice that which can be adequately explained by stupidity. With that in mind, I think the folks in charge of VRChat have fundamentally misunderstood the community's wants. This "feature" is less functional than the existing alternatives, and has actively worsened the user experience compared to the previous avatar menu.

In case the overwhelming feedback is unclear: Please keep the marketplace from obstructing the user's experience. It should be a convenience for those who wish to use it, not an inconvenience for the vast majority who will not.

=== Proposed Design ===

It would make far more sense to include the avatar marketplace in the dedicated marketplace tab already at the bottom of the menu. This would mean that all paid content is easily accessed and managed in one place.

As for the avatar menu, I question why the wheel needs to be re-invented. The previous avatar menu was very functional and easy to use. An addition of a "purchased" section for the avatar marketplace would be the only major change to the previous UI.

== Summary and Postmortem == 

Regardless of the merits of the avatar marketplace as a concept, the fact that this feature was released in such a buggy, poorly thought-out state indicates a failure in the development cycle of this game. Despite being tested and disliked in the open beta, the update was pushed through without regard for their suggestions and feedback. After being released to the general public, more complaints and frustration with these changes have come in, and despite this, the VRChat team has yet to take accountability for their actions and have consistently been deflecting the blame for things such as the loss of functionality of the avatar menu or the default homepage of the avatar tab.

Although I am frustrated with these changes, I have nothing but respect for the people who put their effort and energy into making this platform that so many of us call home. I hope that they, in turn, respect the people who make this platform such a vibrant, active community.

- _jami

details:
This is a feature that might be implemented in the distant future, but it could still be useful for users without Unity or an understanding of Unity, and it could benefit artists, commissioners, and even VRChat staff. Here's how the option would be used.

Prerequisites: VRChat account, VRC+, a texture PNG file, and a purchased avatar

Step 1: Login to vrchat.com with your account to access the homepage.

Step 2: Click on the Inventory tab.

Step 3: Go to the Textures tab, which will be next to the Items tab. Do NOT use the Emoji or Sticker tab, as those can be shared.

Step 4: Follow steps to upload the texture file. Make sure it is a PNG that is 1024 x1024 pixels or less.

Step 5: Enter VRChat and go to the Explore option Avatars menu.

Step 6: Look for your purchased avatar and select Details.

Step 7: Scroll down the Details menu until you see Materials.

Step 8: Select the desired texture slot (Often BaseColor), and click on the uploaded texture.

Step 9: Wait a few minutes for the avatar to update on Windows, Android, and iOS sides.

Step 10: Once avatar is updated, click Change into Avatar, and enjoy your newly textured avatar!

Disclaimer: Avatars should also have the option to opt out of custom texturing if they desire.
title: Add the option for texture slots to purchased avatars in Avatar Marketplace

details:
I would like a feature to allow reduced pricing based on previous purchases.

EX: If a customer buys an avatar from me, and I later add a summer version, I can enable customers who bought the original version a reduced price for the new summer version. 

This is partially circumvented with bundles, but I want options for adding more content to an existing avatar without continuously piling more onto a single avatar, tanking the performance, adding more opportunities for bugs, and widening the gap between that PC and Quest users get/see.

I envision this as a sort of Post-release bundling.

This has multiple benefits for creators and users.

Creator pros:

1. Allows creators to add additional content to older avatars, keeping them fresh and interesting.

2. Makes it easier to keep PC/Quest parity, preventing creators from having to strip features from avatars to fit Quest limits

3. Allows creators to add more options and customization with less chance for bugs.

User pros:

1. Gives a more fair price for Quest users. Right now creators are pricing paced on what PC users get, then stripping away feature for quest users. The prices Quest user pay was not calculated with them in mind in the current landscape.

2. Gives users the opportunity to get more out of their favorite avatars without having to re-purchase things they already own. 

3. Encourages creators to add very differently styles accessories, clothes, and props to avatars, allowing for more creative expression on the user's side.

4. Encourages avatar swaps instead of using one avatar with many toggles/sliders at the cost of performance. This will help all users in an instance.
title: Adjusted avatar prices based on previous purchases
